newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iran has massive arsenal of lethal arms - Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran has massive arsenal of lethal arms - Iraq.

text.p: Iraq's ruling Baath party newspaper al-Thawra said on Friday the United States was encouraging Iran to build an arsenal of weapons of mass destruction to further its interests in the Gulf.
The paper described the U.S. attitude toward Iran's military build-up as "hypocritical", saying Washington wanted Iran to arm itself to blackmail Gulf countries to buy more U.S. arms.

"Iran has embarked since the early 1990s on the building of a massive arsenal of weapons including weapons of mass destruction, long-range missiles and nuclear military programmes with little problem," the paper declared in a commentary.

"Washington is practising clear and overt political hypocrisy in its warnings and rejections of Iran's militarisation policy as it illicitly encourages Iran to go ahead with this policy," the paper said.

It said Tehran's weapons programmes served U.S. interests in the region. The United States, Thawra added, uses the alleged Iranian threat to force Gulf states to buy more of its weapons and agree to the presence of its troops in the area.
It also said a powerful Iran served U.S. interests to weaken Iraq: "The strengthening of the power of the monster (Iran) will turn it into a constant source of threat to Iraq."
Iraq emerged from its 1980-1988 war with Iran as the region's main power with a massive arsenal of chemical weapons, biological arms and long-range missiles.

But it was compelled to scrap the arsenal under the terms that ended its 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait. Iraq is still under U.N. trade sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which bar the purchase of military hardware.
Iran and Iraq have not signed a peace treaty since a U.N.-brokered ceasefire ended hostilities in 1988.
